recordedBy: FOUNDER DIRECTION 2026-08-18 — preserve legacy F133 rows as an explicit OWED production-data remediation item.

newWritesAndProjections.evidence: src/media/duration-units.ts; messages.service.ts write site and projection site both converted; duration-units.spec.ts (15 tests) covers both directions, rounding, null-vs-zero, nonsense refusal and round-trip stability.
newWritesAndProjections.scope: PROSPECTIVE ONLY — applies to writes and projections made after this change.

historicalAffectedRows.mechanism: Media.duration is MILLISECONDS; MessageAttachment.durationSec is SECONDS. messages.service copied one into the other in BOTH directions.
consequence: Rows written through the correspondence attachment path hold a Media.duration that is 1000x TOO SMALL (a 30-second clip stored as 30 instead of 30000).
Those same rows project a durationSec that is 1000x TOO LARGE when read back through the ms-to-seconds site (30000 ms read as 30000 seconds).
historicalAffectedRows.populationSize: NOT MEASURED. Measuring it means querying production, which is not authorized. No count is asserted, and no count is estimated.
historicalAffectedRows.detectability: Nothing crashed and nothing errored. The value was simply wrong wherever it was displayed, which is why the defect survived to become a finding.

remediation.rule: The prospective implementation correction does NOT authorize historical production-data mutation.
remediation.notDesigned: No migration is authored, sketched or planned here. Designing one would make it look scheduled.
remediation.admissionPath: Must be separately ADMITTED and AUTHORIZED through the applicable production-data governance boundary before any migration is written or executed.

verified: No production database read or written.
No existing Media or MessageAttachment row touched by the F133 change — the conversion applies at the write and projection sites only.

whyThisIsHarderThanItLooks.note: Recorded so a future remediation does not begin from a false assumption.
points: A blind multiply-by-1000 would be WRONG. Rows written before the defect existed, rows written through paths that never had the bug, and rows written after this correction all hold CORRECT millisecond values. A remediation must first distinguish affected rows from unaffected ones.

The two error directions are not symmetric: the stored value is wrong, and the projection of an already-correct stored value is also wrong. Only the stored side is data; the projection side was code and is now fixed.

There may be no reliable discriminator in the data itself — a stored 30 could be a genuinely 30 ms clip or a mis-stored 30-second one. Whether the affected population is identifiable at all is an open question, not an assumption.
